is: The private data boundary in PostgreSQL: app-owned rows (actors keyed by their DID, everything else UUIDv7), SQL kept in per-statement files, and typed accessors generated from a live migrated schema.
conventions: SQL never lives in Rust; `query!`/`query_as!` macros are retired by construction (`macros` feature off), and a query's doc text is slimmed in its `.sql` file, never in the generated module.
The EXEMPT list in `tests/it/no_bare_pool_writes.rs` is the authoritative record of the bare-pool write holes — a new exemption is a design question, not a quiet edit.
Migrations only via `just migrate-add <name>` (a hand-typed round-hour version is a latent collision); filename = `<version>_<name>.sql`.
Custody key material is envelope-encrypted (XChaCha20-Poly1305) under a root key before it touches disk.
Table names singular from ZMVP-65 on.

Commission-owned satellite rows that annotate other bookkeeping (e.g. `commission_markup`) are NON-FACT and carry a composite FK back onto their parent row, so a cross-commission reference is unrepresentable.
`FileStore` streams at the port (`AsyncRead` in, `FileDownload` out) but this v1 adapter buffers in memory — a documented exception pending the blob architecture.

Directory name = generated module, file name = generated function, a leading -- comment becomes its doc. Carries no node of its own: sqlx-rust-codegen refuses any non-directory under queries/, so the chart for it lives here.

notes: Module → port: `commission.rs` backs `CommissionStore`/`CommissionWrites`, `workflow.rs` backs `WorkflowStore`/`WorkflowWrites` + `ColumnStore`/`ColumnWrites` (board placement lives here, not in `commission.rs`), `account.rs` backs the account stores/writes.

A node statement's failure, or a refused commission create, ends the unit: `PgUnitOfWork` remembers it and `commit` returns an error, rolling back. PostgreSQL answers COMMIT in a failed transaction with the tag ROLLBACK and no error, and sqlx 0.9 reports that as success. So `commit` also runs one statement on the transaction before COMMIT (`queries::health::is_reachable`): any statement failure that aborted the transaction, even one whose error the caller dropped, makes `commit` roll back and return an error, keeping nothing. The cost is one extra round trip per commit. A refusal that did not abort the transaction (e.g. a not-found answered after a read) is not caught.
DDL lives here and only here: `migrations/` is the schema's one home; no other crate ships SQL.

Fact-anchored deletion is encoded as two constants per aggregate — `{COMMISSION,ACCOUNT}_FACT_TABLES` / `_NON_FACT_TABLES`. Every table with an FK onto `commission(id)` / `accounts(id)` must appear in exactly one list; a schema tripwire test (`tests/it/commission.rs`, `tests/it/account.rs`) enforces it, and a `const_assert`-style guard fails the build when a FACT list gains its first entry (DD 3014657, DD 23003138).
`account.rs::hard_delete` deletes children-first — `account_invitations` → `account_members` → `accounts` (the FKs do not cascade); `account_handle_changes` cascades off the account row.

Composition writes serialize per tab: both the add and the remove path take the shared `require_tab` row lock before touching any element row, so a renumber `UPDATE` cannot race an append's position-assignment subquery.

A departure (`settle_member_departure`, behind `revoke_role` and `leave`) reads the departing member's row `FOR UPDATE` before any write and refuses the Owner, writing nothing, so a transfer to that member either commits first and is read as Owner, or waits for the departure and then finds the row gone. It then revokes the member's pending invitations before re-homing their children, so an accept in flight is either refused or committed first and re-homed, and after its delete it re-homes once more, so a child committed under the member while the departure waited (a member and their parent departing at once) is re-homed too. `create_invitation` reads the issuer's row `FOR KEY SHARE` and refuses an issuer who is not a member, writing nothing, so an issue racing its issuer's departure is either refused or committed first and then revoked by it.

`src/queries.rs` still carries the old pointer-bearing doc text until the next `just gen-queries` picks up the cleaned `.sql` headers. Left as-is deliberately: in-body `--` explainers, `RAISE EXCEPTION` strings inside migration functions, and test-body section dividers are code, not documentation.
Moved migration rationale: Full design-history text trimmed out of oversized migration headers during the 2026-09-12 sweep (Job 1), kept here for anyone who needs the "why," not just the "what."

**`20260630140000_add_account_handle.sql`** — Adds the account's public handle: the validated, normalized atproto handle chosen by the founder at `POST /accounts` (either a Zurfur-issued `<label>.zurfur.app` subdomain or a brought/BYO domain, validated by the domain `Handle` newtype). REQUIRED and UNIQUE; the unique index (`accounts_handle_key`) is GLOBAL — not filtered on `deleted_at` — so a soft-deleted (tombstoned) account still reserves its handle, freed only on hard delete (deliberate: a tombstoned handle must not be silently re-claimable). NOT NULL with no default: every account has always been founded with a handle from this migration onward. The unique index is the store-level backstop the founding handler maps to a 409.

**`20260702000000_plc_operations_no_chain_fork.sql`** — A minted did:plc is a strictly LINEAR chain of operations — every non-genesis op chains onto exactly one `prev` (the CID of the op before it), and a given op may be chained onto at most once. Without this, two concurrent handle updates both read the same `latest_cid` as their `prev`, build different operations, and both append — forking the local chain, permanently disagreeing with the canonical directory's real tip. A partial UNIQUE index over `(did, prev)` makes a non-genesis fork unrepresentable: the losing concurrent writer's INSERT fails, and `update_handle`'s benign-replay guard sees a different tip, propagates the error, and the caller's retry re-reads and chains onto the new tip — serializing concurrent writers into one linear chain. Scoped `WHERE prev IS NOT NULL` because a genesis op has `prev = NULL` and is already one-per-DID by construction.

**`20260707000000_add_maturity_commission.sql`** — Two nullable envelope columns on the commission row (like deadline, not a tree/tab node). `maturity` is the four-tier axis token ('safe'|'suggestive'|'nudity'|'adult'); `graphic` is the orthogonal Graphic flag (gore is not a sexual-maturity question), meaningful only alongside a rating. Both start NULL for every commission: a commission is born unrated by invariant (birth commissions are Private/root-Total, so nobody outside can see anything yet). The rating becomes REQUIRED at the widening gate — "cannot widen to non-participants unrated." The CHECK makes a half-set posture unrepresentable: rated = both columns, unrated = neither.

**`20260910193912_drop_superseded_placement_tables.sql`** — Drops the superseded account-level placement rails. `commission_placement` and its denormalized `commission_current_placement` pointer were an append-only log with exactly one CURRENT account per commission — the shape of a managing-account assignment log that Ownership Separation superseded in favor of "placement = workflow membership rows, account-side." So placement was never a second thing; it is a card in a column (`workflow_column_commission`), which is also why one commission can sit on N accounts' boards with no conflict. Nothing reads or writes the dropped tables any more. **Drop, not migrate** — pre-alpha, no real data to carry across, and a row here names no board/column in the new model.

**`20260630190000_create_account_keys_table.sql`** — Custody store for the private keys behind a minted account did:plc. When Zurfur mints an account's sovereign identity it generates per-account secp256k1 keypairs (a cold-recovery key, an operational key, and an atproto signing key) and must keep the private halves to operate the DID. These are the most sensitive rows Zurfur holds, so every key is envelope-encrypted under a root key held outside the database (config/env in v1; a cloud KMS is a planned follow-up) — a database compromise alone yields no usable key material.

**`20260705200000_create_commission_placement_and_view_grant.sql`** — Two account-facing rails that replaced the deleted managing-account concept: Users own commissions, accounts own positioning, and NEITHER rail confers any in-commission authority. Placement is account-side (an append-only log plus a denormalized current-placement pointer, upserted in the same unit of work as each log append); the view grant is a commission-side key that NEVER shares a table with placement. Both are commission-owned bookkeeping, not facts, so they cascade away with the commission and (via `ON DELETE CASCADE`) with the account, never blocking either deletion. The view grant HARD-DELETES on revoke (no soft-deleted rows); its history lives only in the changelog. (Both tables were later dropped — see `20260910193912_drop_superseded_placement_tables.sql`.)

**`20260907060908_rekey_actors_on_did.sql`** — Until this migration an actor had two names: a surrogate UUIDv7 row key and the `did:plc` everything public already used. This migration collapses them: `users.id` and `accounts.id` become the DID text, and every column that pointed at an actor by UUID is retyped to carry the DID instead (Bluesky's own PDS/AppView/Ozone key their actor tables the same way). DATA-PRESERVING: nothing is dropped or invented — `actor_identity` already holds the (id → did) map for every actor, so every UUID in the schema can be rewritten to the DID it already stood for; a helper function does that lookup once and RAISEs loudly, naming the offending UUID, rather than inventing a value if an actor ever fails to resolve. WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE: `actor_identity` keeps its own `id uuid PRIMARY KEY` — re-keying it is a domain change (the domain still models `ActorIdentityId` as a UUID newtype), not an adapter one; the projections' parent constraint is instead repointed at the natural key, `users (id, kind) → actor_identity (did, kind)`.

**`20260805234354_flat_commission_composition.sql`** — Retires the recursive `commission_node` adjacency tree and replaces it with three fixed-depth tables (`commission_tab`, `commission_element`, `commission_surface_mode`) and no parent pointers anywhere: depth is fixed by the model (commission > tab > surface > element), so effective visibility is `min(tab.mode, surface_mode, element.mode)` — three lookups, zero recursion. Surface STRUCTURE is code (a global invariant skeleton in Rust); surface MODES are data, and only once widened past the default (absent row = Total). **Drop-and-recreate, not a data migration** — pre-alpha, no real data: existing dev databases keep their commissions and every envelope fact, but lose their tree content, declared Slots/Seats, every seat invitation, and every non-owner participant row. The skeleton (tab rows) is backfilled so "a commission always has its tab state" holds for old rows too. Membership dies with the seats that justified it: dropping every Seat drops every justification for non-owner membership (a participant row is the key to the closed door `is_participant` checks), so the residue is swept — the owner's permanent floor row survives (it never came from a Seat), and everyone else re-earns membership through seat-invitation acceptance from a seat that actually exists. Slot and Seat became identity-sharing satellites keyed on the element id via a COMPOSITE foreign key `(element id, commission_id) → commission_element (id, commission_id)`, making a satellite that claims a different commission than its own element unrepresentable at the database rather than merely unwritten.

**`20261012014616_delete_stored_oauth_sessions.sql`** — Sign-in used to ask for `atproto transition:generic`, so every stored OAuth session may hold a token that writes to the visitor's repo, and every pending sign-in asks for one. This migration empties both tables once, with TRUNCATE, and touches nothing else; Zurfur's own login sessions (`tower_sessions.session`) are kept and nothing reads a stored OAuth session, so nobody is signed out, while a sign-in in flight fails at its callback and is started again. Why a migration, not a one-off command: the API runs every migration at boot, and sqlx refuses to start a build on a database that has applied a migration the build doesn't carry. So once a database has run it, an older build that still asks for write access can no longer start on that database. It does not stop a backend that is already running: stop every backend on the database before the new build first starts. Every checkout sharing that database (the dev `localhost:5432/zurfur`) refuses to boot until it carries this migration. Why TRUNCATE, not DELETE: the tables get new, empty files and the old ones are emptied at commit, instead of the rows lingering as dead row versions until a vacuum; the WAL and any backup still hold them. Most rows are sealed under the root key; rows written before the store sealed them are plaintext, and go the same way. Without CASCADE it fails, rather than spreads, if anything ever references these tables.

**`20261022052438_create_node.sql`** — The Den's node table (key, real parent, segment, type, level, name) and its first rows: each commission's node, its six fixed entries and its Slots' nodes, with `node_id` set on every commission and Slot row. Why every DDL statement runs first: PostgreSQL refuses to ALTER a table with pending trigger events (`CheckTableNotInUse`, `tablecmds.c`), and the backfill's UPDATE statements queue deferred foreign-key and constraint-trigger events on `commission` and `commission_slot`; so the table, the columns, the functions and the triggers all exist before the DO check and the backfill. Why deferred keys: a commission or Slot and its node are written in one unit in either order, and one created and deleted in the same unit commits, so the `node_id` foreign keys and `node_matches_its_thing` check at commit; the parent key, the CHECKs and the BEFORE triggers stay immediate. Why v4 ids for the backfilled rows: they have no creation instant of their own to sort by, and `gen_random_uuid()` is core; nodes the app mints stay UUIDv7. Atomic: `no_tx` false, so sqlx runs the file and its ledger row in one transaction, and a refusal leaves no table, column or ledger row. Nothing is repaired: a commission whose visibility isn't exactly private, listed or public, or whose title is empty, stops the migration naming its id and the column, echoing neither value. A title the name rule would refuse is still copied verbatim.

Node guards and their precedents: `node_keeps_its_place` (BEFORE UPDATE OF id, parent, segment, type; the `commission_changelog` append-only precedent) refuses a move, a re-segment or a retype, while a name or level update passes. `node_fits_its_parent` (BEFORE INSERT) puts an entry only under a `commission` node and a slot only under a `commission.slots` node; a parent the statement can't see yet counts as the wrong type, and a node with no parent is left to `node_top_level_is_a_commission`. `node_entry_stays_with_its_commission` (BEFORE DELETE of a fixed entry; the `commission_participant` owner-floor precedent) refuses while the entry's parent lives, and the cascade from a deleted commission node runs after that node is gone, so it passes. `node_id_is_set_once` lets `node_id` go from NULL to a node once. `node_matches_its_thing` (a deferred constraint trigger on insert and on the key columns) checks at commit that a commission points at a top-level `commission` node whose segment is its id, and a Slot at a `slot` node whose segment is its element id under its own commission's `commission.slots` entry; it returns quietly for a row deleted since. `node_follows_its_thing` (AFTER DELETE) deletes a deleted commission's or Slot's node, and the parent key's cascade takes its subtree; a row with no node deletes nothing. Every RAISE names ids only, never a title, name, segment or token. Not here: the check that a row points at each `commission` and `slot` node, which the commission and Slot slices own.

`node_follows_a_truncate`: a statement-level AFTER TRUNCATE trigger on `commission` and on `commission_slot` deletes every node of that type (`commission`, `slot`). `TRUNCATE commission CASCADE` empties `commission_slot` too and both fire; the parent key's cascade takes the entries, whose guard passes because their parent is already gone. A BEFORE TRUNCATE refusal was declined: it would block a deliberate full wipe. A TRUNCATE in a unit that still has pending deferred trigger events on the table fails, so a test seeds and commits first, then truncates in a fresh unit.

The widened ALTER rule: a migration that writes `commission`, `commission_slot` or `node` rows doesn't ALTER (or TRUNCATE) any of the three afterwards in the same file. Deferred foreign-key and constraint-trigger events pending on a table make a later ALTER of it fail ("cannot ALTER TABLE … because it has pending trigger events").

Row values stay out of PostgreSQL's log: the dev database runs `log_error_verbosity = terse`, which drops a violation's DETAIL ("Failing row contains …") from the server log. As a second line, a backfill or re-sync checks every constraint its writes can hit before writing: `create_node`'s DO check covers `node_level_known` and `node_name_not_empty`, ids always fit the segment rule, and Slot titles are already held non-blank by a CHECK.

Migration headers that say `See NODE.md ("<file>")` or "this crate's NODE.json notes" mean this node: the moved rationale sits in these notes, keyed by migration filename. The headers stay byte-for-byte as shipped because sqlx checksums every migration on boot.

`src/character.rs`: `PgCharacterStore::list_kept_by` answers an empty list — a named exemption from "no stubs", because no Character can be stored in PostgreSQL yet (`create` is `unimplemented!`). A unit test (`src/character/tests.rs`) pins it; the slice that adds character storage replaces both as one of its acceptance criteria.

Standing reads (`queries/commission/standing.sql`, `standing_for_update.sql`): the pool statement is a one-row `VALUES` probe left-joined to `commission`, so an absent id and a stranger run one statement with one row shape and one participant probe; it decodes only lenient columns (`stored_level`, `archived_flag`). The locked read is two statements on the unit: `standing_for_update` locks the commission row (`FOR NO KEY UPDATE OF commission`), then `is_participant` probes. The probe can't sit inside the locking statement: under READ COMMITTED a subquery reads the snapshot taken before the lock was granted, so it would miss an eviction committed while the lock was awaited (pinned by `standing_for_update_sees_a_change_committed_while_it_waited`).

A commission create (`create_commission.sql`) inserts from the gate's node row: a top-level `commission` node whose segment is the id. Any other node inserts no row, and `PgCommissionWrites::create` errs on a count other than one. A zero-row insert aborts nothing, so the create sets the unit's failure memory (the node view's latch) itself: the unit's later node calls fail and its commit rolls back.
